summary: SELENE is an interactive web explorer that helps plan lunar missions by finding and comparing landing sites, with a focus on the Moon's South Pole. Users pick a curated site (Shackleton, Malapert, Cabeus, IM-1, Chandrayaan-3, Chang'e 4, Apollo 11) or any point of their own, set a mission date and duration, and SELENE computes hour by hour when the site has sunlight and when it has direct line of sight to Earth for communications. The calculations use Sun and Earth positions from NASA/JPL Horizons and the real topographic horizon built from LRO LOLA elevation data. The results appear on 2D and 3D maps, an illumination heat map, side-by-side site comparisons and a printable report that cites its sources. This addresses the challenge directly: light means power and heat, Earth visibility means communication, and terrain means safety. These three factors decide whether a South Pole mission like Artemis can succeed. By turning raw NASA datasets into clear, verifiable answers, SELENE lets students, teams and planners compare candidate sites in minutes instead of days.
details:
What exactly does it do?

SELENE is a web application designed to identify and compare potential landing sites on the Moon, especially near the South Pole. It analyzes sunlight availability, communication opportunities with Earth, and lunar terrain conditions.

Using interactive maps and 3D models, it helps users determine the most suitable locations and dates for future lunar missions, considering energy, communication, and safety.

How does it work?

SELENE is a web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its main objective is to analyze and compare potential landing sites on the Moon, especially in the Moon's South Pole region.

The platform allows users to select different locations, set mission dates and durations, and study the environmental conditions of each site. To achieve this, it combines astronomical and topographical data to evaluate two essential factors: solar energy availability and direct communication opportunities with Earth.

Through its interactive tools, SELENE displays the lunar surface using 2D maps and 3D models. It also allows users to visualize the terrain, observe the positions of the Sun and Earth, and analyze how these conditions change over time. Additionally, it includes comparison features that help evaluate different locations and identify which ones offer better conditions for a future mission.

SELENE uses data from NASA sources such as JPL Horizons, LOLA, and LROC, which provide information about astronomical positions, lunar elevations, and surface images.

In conclusion, SELENE aims to support the planning of future lunar missions through a visual and interactive tool that helps identify and compare potential landing sites, considering important factors such as solar illumination, communication with Earth, and terrain characteristics.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

In this project, we decided to use the following coding languages: HTML, JavaScript, and CSS. We chose them because we had already worked with them, both in high school and in personal projects, so we knew what we were dealing with. To develop it, we used Visual Studio Code to write the code, Vite and three.js to build the website and its 3D Moon, Figma to design the interface, and GitHub to keep a smooth workflow among the team's coders. We also used AI coding agents like Claude Code CLI, Codex, and OpenCode. They were very helpful in understanding how to connect the resources NASA gave us with the code we developed. The website is hosted on Vercel, and we used our personal laptops, so no special hardware was needed.

What do you hope to achieve?

Our objective is to win an important competition like this one by creating a meaningful tool. We also hope to break down the barriers between countries by helping develop new ways to support scientists and astronauts, because for teenagers like us, it is hard to reach unknown fields from Uruguay.

What benefits does it have?

With this software, you have access to an important source of information that is available not only to everyone but also to NASA. This makes it a global application for anyone who is interested.
